# ScopeGate

> ScopeGate is an open-source (Apache-2.0) ephemeral-credentials gateway for coding agents — Claude Code, Kimi Code, Cursor, OpenCode, and any MCP-capable harness. The agent never holds secrets; it holds short-lived, minimum-scope capabilities. Real secrets live in an AES-256-GCM encrypted local vault and are injected only at the outbound hop, so a leaked model context leaks nothing of durable value. Think of it as AWS IAM + STS for coding agents, installable by the agent itself in under 90 seconds.

## Product

- [Landing](https://scopegate.io/): What ScopeGate is, the two structural failures it fixes (secret exposure in model context, OAuth expiration mid-session), and how it works.
- [Quickstart](https://scopegate.io/docs/quickstart): Zero to first proxied tool call; fully agent-executable and non-interactive (`npm i -g scopegate && scopegate init`).
- [Security model](https://scopegate.io/docs/security-model): The enforcement rules — capability ≠ credential, write asymmetry (agents propose, humans approve), fail-closed hard limits, signed audit.
- [Agent protocol](https://scopegate.io/docs/agent-protocol): The SKILL protocol agents follow to self-operate the gateway.
- [CLI reference](https://scopegate.io/docs/cli-reference): Every `scopegate` command and flag.
- [Configuration](https://scopegate.io/docs/configuration): `scopegate.yaml`, `policies.yaml`, environment variables.

## Agent guides (self-install, self-operate)

- [Agent guides index](https://scopegate.io/docs/agents/): Who the docs are for and how to consume them.
- [01 — Quickstart: self-install](https://scopegate.io/docs/agents/01-quickstart-self-install): Detect, install and initialize ScopeGate non-interactively; the single human step (depositing secrets).
- [02 — Protocol](https://scopegate.io/docs/agents/02-protocol): The capability lifecycle — request → grant → use → expire; what `pending_human_approval` means.
- [03 — Tools reference](https://scopegate.io/docs/agents/03-tools-reference): The twenty-one `scopegate_*` MCP tools with exact parameters, return shapes and copy-paste JSON payloads.
- [04 — Connectors](https://scopegate.io/docs/agents/04-connectors): Native bridges (Huly 16 tools, Railway 7, Cloudflare 8, Google 7, GitHub App), the OpenAPI importer and custom MCP upstreams.
- [05 — Policies](https://scopegate.io/docs/agents/05-policies): Capability matching, TTL rules, hard limits, and how to propose a policy a human can approve fast.
- [06 — Self-repair](https://scopegate.io/docs/agents/06-self-repair): The diagnose-first playbook for auth/connection errors.
- [07 — Security rules](https://scopegate.io/docs/agents/07-security-rules): The non-negotiables and how ScopeGate enforces them.

## Facts

- Open source, Apache-2.0. Gateway is local-first: the cloud management plane is optional and metadata-only (it never receives secret values).
- Twenty-one MCP tools: `scopegate_request_capability`, `scopegate_request_capabilities` (batch), `scopegate_list_capabilities`, `scopegate_register_upstream`, `scopegate_diagnose`, `scopegate_propose_policy`, `scopegate_vault_status`, `scopegate_collect`, `scopegate_wait`, `scopegate_upstream_health`, `scopegate_can_i`, `scopegate_policy_summary`, `scopegate_recall`, `scopegate_events`, `scopegate_open_task_lease`, `scopegate_renew_capability`, `scopegate_request_plan`, `scopegate_result_get`, `scopegate_result_grep`, `scopegate_delegate`, `scopegate_inject_file`.
- Delegation: `scopegate_delegate` issues attenuated child grants for subagents (scope ⊆ parent, ttl ≤ parent remaining, fail-closed on widening), with the full attribution chain — revoking the parent kills every child.
- Taint tracking: upstream responses are scored for prompt injection; a tainted payload marks the session (30 min) and, in enforce mode, cross-upstream writes degrade to human approval automatically.
- Hot-reload: `scopegate secret add` while the gateway runs drops stale connections and re-injects fresh credentials on the next call — no agent-session restart, no context loss; config changes emit `tools/list_changed`.
- Capability plans: `scopegate_request_plan` submits the whole task at once — auto-approvable capabilities are issued immediately, denials reported, and every guarded capability is bundled into ONE aggregated human approval with the full blast radius visible.
- Result handles: proxied payloads over limits.max_inline_bytes (default 16 KiB) are persisted (after policy redaction) and returned as preview + `result_ref` + stats; the agent pages with `scopegate_result_get` (dot-path) and searches with `scopegate_result_grep` — the context window is never flooded.
- Task leases: `scopegate_open_task_lease` groups a task's grants under a double budget (total time, hard-clamped by limits.max_lease_total default 4h; write count); the agent renews grants itself with `scopegate_renew_capability` (sliding TTL, never past the deadline) and gets a structured warning at <20% TTL.
- Idempotent writes: `_sg_idempotency_key` on any proxied call — same key + same args replays the cached result (upstream untouched, 24h); same key + different args is an explicit conflict error.
- Approval continuation: `execute_on_approval` queues the intended call; the gateway executes it the moment the human approves (CLI or panel) and the agent collects the outcome with `scopegate_collect`/`scopegate_wait` — no polling loops, no abandoned tasks.
- Approval wait: `wait: true` on `scopegate_request_capability` long-polls the human decision inline (max 120 s) and returns the grant in the same call (`via: "human_approval"`) — or `denied` / `approval_timeout`; every wait is audited (`approval_waited`).
- Pluggable approval channels: Slack incoming webhooks, generic HMAC-SHA256-signed webhooks and Huly via `notify.json notifiers[]`; approval decisions are pushed back to the same channels.
- Arg-aware policies: `when:` clauses on capability rules guard the call's arguments (picomatch globs for strings, strict equality for numbers/booleans) — e.g. pushes to `kimi/*` branches auto-approve while `main` escalates; the guard sticks to the issued grant.
- Git credential helper: `scopegate git-credential` is a native git credential-helper — `git credential fill` gets a freshly minted GitHub App installation token (capability `git:credential:<path>` governed by the same policy engine, audit kind `git_credential_minted`); tokens never sit in remote URLs or `.git/config`.
- Multi-identity HTTP gateway: the `X-ScopeGate-Agent` header selects the logical agent per request (validated against the policies allowlist, 403 otherwise) — one gateway serves many threads/tasks with separate grants, audit trails and approval queues.
- Batch capability requests: `scopegate_request_capabilities {requests: [...]}` (max 20) returns per-item granted/pending/denied outcomes with a single rate-limit evaluation.
- Governed file injection: `scopegate inject --ref <ref> --out <path> [--template ...]` and the `scopegate_inject_file` tool materialize a vault secret into a legacy config file — human approval BY DEFAULT (`vault:inject:<ref>` inverted default), atomic 0600 write with backup, sha256-only audit, `--refresh` re-materializes after rotation.
- Host observability: `scopegate_events` (MCP tool) and `GET /events` (NDJSON) expose a metadata-only event tail; `/health` carries readiness detail (upstreams ok/failed, vault mode, pending approvals); upstream state changes push MCP `notifications/message`.
- Embeddable library API: `import { createGatewayServer } from "scopegate"` boots the gateway in-process (no subprocess, no daemons); `scopegate/testkit` ships a fake upstream + `bootFakeGateway()` for consumer integration tests without real credentials.
- Any REST API as a governed upstream: the `openapi` transport generates one governed MCP tool per operation from an OpenAPI 3 spec (https or local file) — no custom bridge needed.
- Huly connector at full parity: 16 tools — read issue with description, read comments, edit message, thinking flag, assignee filter, milestone/dueDate, status on create.
- Honeytoken CLI: `scopegate honeytoken plant <name>` deposits a decoy credential whose use triggers surgical revocation.
- Policy preflight: `scopegate_can_i` answers allow|needs_approval|deny with zero side effects, and `scopegate_policy_summary` is the session-start digest — plan the task instead of learning from denials.
- Agent recall: `scopegate_recall` exposes the agent's own signed audit as session memory (recent actions, writes, active grants, pending approvals) — scoped to its agentId only.
- Machine-readable error envelopes on every failure: `{kind, next_action, retry_after_s?}` with a per-upstream circuit breaker (fail-fast after 5 consecutive failures).
- Token minter: gateway JWTs, GitHub App installation tokens, AWS STS, Google service-account tokens, Huly workspace tokens.
- Signed audit trail: append-only, hash-chained, Ed25519-signed JSONL; inputs are hashed, never stored.
- Fleet revocation via the cloud panel is effective in under 30 seconds on online gateways; offline agents' tokens expire by TTL anyway.
